topic.source_contract: Assets of Community Value and Community Right to Bid evidence

facts.law: Localism Act 2011 community right to bid framework
facts.guard: statutory listing is not community ownership or a planning designation
regulatory process must be matched to current local-list status

sources.publisher: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames

facts.scheme: qualifying groups nominate assets; listed disposal triggers moratorium
facts.guard: listing does not force an owner to sell to a community group
moratorium is an opportunity to bid, not first refusal or price control

facts.proposal: future Community Right to Buy reform
facts.guard: bill proposal is not current enacted purchase right

scope_guards: An Asset of Community Value listing is not freehold title or community ownership.
Nomination, listing, review, appeal and removal are distinct stages.
A listed asset does not give a community group a right of first refusal under the current scheme.
The six-week interim and six-month full moratorium are sale-process periods, not purchase guarantees.
The owner can choose whether and to whom to sell after the applicable moratorium.
ACV listing is not planning permission, public access, compulsory acquisition or a use restriction by itself.
Proposed Community Right to Buy reforms are not applied before enactment and commencement.
No score or promotion is written without exact local list, listing dates, disposal notice, moratorium, review/appeal, title and planning evidence.
